headline: SHORT ORDER SHOUT ships — a co-op kitchen where every seat takes orders
lede: Issue #1248 asked for an Overcooked-style game as original IP with voice from day one. Session 61 built the diner: deterministic tickets, a split-firewall counter that makes handoffs the fast path, and four seats any of which a human, a CPU, or later a model can fill.

notes.text: SHORT ORDER SHOUT shipped (#1248): 1-4 cooks run a 13x7 diner on order timers — boil, melt, douse fires, rinse plates, serve across the pass counter. Solo wins are ~15 percent tighter than duo, so the partner is load-bearing. Live at /retrogames/short-order-shout.

Model-ready from day one (#494, #1247): every seat is a pure deterministic slot (seeded, per-tick hash) with 2x5 sensors and a sos.calls voice channel, all recorded by rec/v2; no-op pads stay 0 so a trained agent can take a seat without touching the sim.

Two new checks: soscheck, 36 gates pinning rules, determinism and the solo-slack proof; sosplay, 11 gates driving real keyboard events with pixel/state agreement. Mutant-proven - neuter the boil-over rule and the gate goes red.
Staged on purpose: online kitchen lobby filed as #1291 (the sim is lockstep-ready - remote input is just pads[seat]) and the polish pass as #1292.
